samples.question: The picture is a row of four square panels showing the same scene at four successive moments. Read the panels in order from left to right, as the grey arrow below them shows. Each panel contains five discs, and the five discs are the same five objects in every panel: an object moves only a short way from one panel to the next. Positions are read inside each panel, that is, relative to that panel's own frame, because every panel frames the same square scene. To follow an object from one panel to the next, take the disc in the next panel whose place inside its panel is nearest to the place the object had inside the previous panel; the picture is always drawn so that this nearest-place matching is unambiguous and pairs the five discs one to one. Colour does not follow an object: the five colours blue, green, orange, purple and yellow are dealt out afresh in every panel, so each panel shows each colour exactly once but an object may wear a different colour in every panel. A black ring is drawn in the first panel only, and it marks one object: the marked object is the one whose disc centre is nearest to the centre of that ring. The ring is drawn only in the first panel and never moves with the object. Which colour is the marked object wearing in the fourth panel, the rightmost one? Answer with one of blue, green, orange, purple or yellow.
